Hi Akira —

Thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap of needs you mentioned:
- In-product summarization and smart search (embedding + reranker flow).
- Strict data residency + VPC-only agent access for internal docs.
- Deterministic structured outputs for downstream systems (JSON schema/field validation).
- Low-latency requirement for user-facing features (95th pctl < 200ms target).

Technical items we should resolve before a PoC:
1) SDK & auth: which environment will host inference requests? (VPC/private vs Redwood hosted). We'll propose both flows — API key + mTLS for Hosted, IAM + private link for Dedicated/Private.
2) Routing & model selection: we recommend an inference policy (latency-first for interactive, cost-first for batch emb).
3) Structured output & tool calling: confirm preferred schema for your summarizer output and what external tools we should call (e.g., internal search API).
4) Embeddings & reranker: typical pattern is periodic index refresh + on-call reranker for recall/precision tradeoffs.
5) Prompt governance: versioned system prompts, a small red-team test tranche, and injection mitigation (canonicalize inputs, allowlist tools).

Attachments I’m including: preliminary architecture sketch and a sample prompt set we discussed.
[Attachment: ndp-arch-v1.png (image/png)]
[Attachment: sample-prompts.csv (text/csv)]

Proposed next steps (pick from these):
- Technical deep-dive with your infra & security teams (60m) — suggest Tue 11/24 or Thu 11/26 (APAC morning / Redwood late-night UTC-8).
- Provide a short anonymized dataset (5–10k docs) we can index for a PoC.
- Redwood to share an MSA/PSA draft for legal review (we can use DocuSign).

If you confirm the deep-dive slot I’ll loop in Monica (CS) to scope the PoC milestones and Marissa to own the architecture details.

Cheers,

Hi Akira / Priya —

Great — confirmed Tue 11/24 09:30 JST for the deep-dive. I’ll cover runtime, auth, and routing; Monica will cover PoC success metrics. A few technical notes to prep your infra team: 

1) Networking (Dedicated):
- We support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. Typical requirements: outbound NAT for model pull (one-time), allowlist Redwood control-plane IPs for webhook callbacks, and 443 outbound for telemetry (optional).
- If you need a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment, we can share an on-prem bundle but that’s a longer engagement.

2) SDK & auth quick options:
- Hosted: API key rotated via our Console.
- Dedicated/Private: short-lived tokens via your IdP (OIDC) + optional mTLS for service-to-service.

3) Embeddings & reranker pattern:
- Redwood hosts dense embeddings; we can either:
  a) index on Redwood-managed vector store (recommended for speed), or
  b) export vectors to your index (you manage).
- We recommend a two-stage pipeline: semantic recall (embeddings) -> lightweight reranker using a smaller LLM (low cost) -> optional ranker LLM for final pass.

4) Structured output & tool-calling:
- Function-calling / structured output: we suggest schema-first definitions (JSON Schema) and a validation layer at the Redwood SDK client.
- For downstream system integration, we can emit canonical JSON + a change log for schema evolution.

5) Prompt governance (high-level proposal):
- Versioned prompts: use numeric versioning (v1.0, v1.1) stored in our Console with notes and rollouts.
- Approval workflow: small-team approvals (owner + security) before promo to production.
- Prompt-injection mitigations: input normalization, tool call allowlist, and explicit system message allowlist.
- Red-team: schedule a 2-week red-team window during the PoC (we’ll provide attack patterns).

Attachments: updated arch sketch reflecting Dedicated networking and a draft NDA we can sign before exchanging production-like docs.
[Attachment: ndp-arch-v2.png (image/png)]
[Attachment: nda-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

- Indicate whether you want Redwood to host the vector index (we’ll size infra for expected load).

I’ll add these items to the deep-dive agenda.
